newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says STL loading system beats bad weather.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says STL loading system beats bad weather.

text.p: Offshore crude loadings at the Heidrun oilfield in the Norwegian Sea off mid-Norway have continued as normal despite bad weather due to a submerged turret loading (STL) system, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.

When using the STL system, shuttle tankers require a small weather window to connect to the buoy. Once in place, they can remain attached in all kinds of weather until their tanks are full, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.

A similar system also is used on Britain's Harding field and has been adopted for storage ships on the Norwegian North Sea Yme and U.K. sector Fulmar developments. Statoil said Fulmar's Vinga storage tanker has operated for three years without once being forced away by storms.

Offshore loadings at the North Sea Statfjord and Gullfaks installations are often disrupted during winter due to severe winds and high swell. Prolonged delays to loadings often lead to cuts in production due to burgeoning storage capacity.
Three shuttle tankers -- Jorunn Knutsen, Hanne Knutsen and Randgrid -- serve on the Heidrun field.
